# Temporal-pyramid L3–L5 dynamic synthesis path (weekly/monthly/quarterly)

## Context

Leaf C of Epic neomjs/neo-agent-brain#145's implementation decomposition (map: https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/issues/145#issuecomment-4862079789). Filed pre-`Accepted` per ADR 0005 §2.3. Sequenced **after Leaves A (`#14433`) + B (`#14434`)** — synthesis reads L2 aggregates.

**⛔ Merge gate:** merge-blocked until ADR 0028 is `Accepted` (PR `#14428`), per `#11376` §6 and ADR 0028 §5.

## The Problem

*"What happened this week / month / quarter?"* has no cheap answer path. The graduated design answers it with **query-time synthesis** over the durable tiers — deliberately NOT precomputed, so the photocopy-of-a-photocopy degradation and the tier×partition cron explosion never exist.

## The Architectural Reality

Bound by ADR 0028 (re-verify `Accepted` at claim):

- **§2.2:** L3 (weekly) / L4 (monthly) / L5 (quarterly) are computed on demand over L2 aggregates + `query_recent_turns` (chronological) + `query_raw_memories` (semantic). **No durable output above L2** — nothing this leaf produces is written back as summary-of-summary. (The Gemini-family objection incorporated as the Cycle-3 shape; liveness carry in ADR §8.)
- **§2.5 fidelity:** higher tiers cite sessions `impact >= 90` and accepted ADRs **directly**; PR fidelity via named sources (accepted-ADR links / epic labels / high-impact review metadata). No invented universal PR impact score.
- **Query-time cost:** the corrected Cycle-3 math (~33–34 LLM calls/week) is the accepted budget — re-verify at implementation (ADR §4).
- **Surface boundary:** includes only the **minimal Memory Core query entry point** that invokes synthesis. Dashboards, cockpit panes, and richer consumer surfaces stay out (epic Out-of-scope; #11375 territory).
- **ADR §6 consume-direction (pre-declared):** once the `#14422` shared tier contract lands, synthesis over weak-digest sessions propagates a fidelity signal using that contract — adopt, don't invent.

## The Fix

One PR: the L3–L5 synthesis path (window resolution → L2 + recency + semantic retrieval → cited synthesis with §2.5 fidelity rules) + the minimal MC query entry. No scheduled jobs, no durable writes, no consumer UI.

## Decision Record impact

`depends-on ADR 0028` (Accepted-gate) · consumes Leaves A (`#14433`) + B (`#14434`) · future-adopts the `#14422` tier contract (ADR §6 consume-direction).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] L3/L4/L5 windows synthesize on demand over L2 + `query_recent_turns` + `query_raw_memories`; **no durable artifact above L2 is written** (asserted by test).
- [ ] §2.5 fidelity enforced: impact≥90 session citation + accepted-ADR direct-citation + named PR sources.
- [ ] Per-agent + unified partition views honored (§2.6) at synthesis time.
- [ ] Minimal MC query entry point shipped; no dashboard/cockpit surface included.
- [ ] Query-time cost measured against the ~33–34 calls/week budget and recorded in the PR.
- [ ] PR held un-merge-ready until ADR 0028 `Accepted`; gate stated in the PR body.
- [ ] Cross-family review before merge.

## Out of Scope

- Durable precompute of any higher tier (anti-anchor). Consumer surfaces beyond the minimal entry (#11375). The `#14422` vocabulary work itself (adopt-when-landed only). Schema (A) and aggregation (B).

## Avoided Traps

- **Durable L3–L5 cascade** — rejected (photocopy degradation; the design's own center).
- **Per-tier crons** — rejected (batch-explosion; dynamic-by-design).
- **Inventing a provenance vocabulary before `#14422` lands** — rejected (ADR §6: adopt the shared contract; don't fork a dialect).

## Peer-role intake — right P0 lane; six contract corrections before implementation

**Verdict:** neomjs/neo#14435 is the correct Memory/session runtime Bird View lane, and the zero-durable-L3–L5 boundary is sound. The current claim still carries one stale gate and two retrieval assumptions that would let a concise answer masquerade as a complete one.

### Live V-B-A ledger

- **ADR 0028 is already Accepted by its own lifecycle rule.** PR neomjs/neo#14428 is `APPROVED`, all checks on exact head `b60a0668...` succeeded, and it merged at `2026-07-02T06:36:42Z`. ADR 0028 says Proposed becomes Accepted on approved+green human merge. The Markdown header is stale; neomjs/neo#14435's PR must not present itself as un-merge-ready on this gate.
- The actual durable foundation is now **PR neomjs/neo#15016 / neomjs/neo#14938**, merged `2026-07-11T12:45:52Z`, after neomjs/neo#14433/#14434 closed. Memory Core session `d6f084eb-c9bc-4551-8e2e-2bfed6a927aa` preserves that implementation/review arc.
- The landed L1/L2 records are deterministic velocity facts, not narrative summaries. In particular, L1 `level:"session"` is an **hour-aligned clock window**, not a session-id partition; valid partitions are exactly `unified` or a canonical `@<identity>`.
- `query_recent_turns` is exhaustive only if its compound `nextCursor {timestamp,id}` is walked to exhaustion; each call is capped at 100 and selects one agent identity.
- `query_raw_memories` is relevance-ranked semantic search, capped at 100, with no exhaustive chronological cursor. It is valuable enrichment, but it cannot prove source completeness for a time window.

### Required convergence

1. **Pin the runtime operation now.** “Minimal MC query entry” is too vague for the operator's P0 requirement. Ship a distinct read-only operation, provisionally `explore_memory_history`, accepting one normalized half-open window or a named preset plus `partition: "unified" | "@<identity>"`. It must remain separate from neomjs/neo#15088's `explore_pull_request_history`.

2. **Separate admission from prominence.** ADR 0028's `impact >= 90` rule requires direct citation/prominence for high-impact sessions; it must not become an admission filter that silently drops lower-impact sessions from the selected window. First establish the complete session/turn manifest for the requested window, then use impact/semantic relevance to choose what the concise narrative foregrounds.

3. **Make a chronological/exact source the coverage spine.** Enumerate every selected session summary and exhaust every required recency page (with cross-agent de-duplication for `unified`) or report explicit degradation. Use `query_raw_memories` to recover semantic/theme evidence, never as the completeness backbone. L1/L2 counts may cross-check coverage and supply velocity facts; they cannot supply “what happened” prose.

4. **Return useful evidence even when inference fails.** Every response needs a deterministic envelope before any model synthesis:
   - normalized window/preset + filter-set declaration;
   - partition;
   - discovered/included/excluded session and turn counts;
   - exhaustion/missing-source/degraded reasons;
   - source manifest/hash;
   - session + memory/turn drill-down ids;
   - `generatedAt`, citations, and `notAuthority:true`.

   If the narrative provider is unavailable or the source is incomplete, preserve the manifest/coverage and mark synthesis `unavailable|degraded`; never return partial prose as a complete Bird View.

5. **Share mechanics with neomjs/neo#15088, not truth semantics.** The reusable primitive may own window normalization, the coverage/provenance envelope, citation validation, and the inference/chunking adapter. Memory/session enumeration and privacy stay here. Resolved-PR selection, resolution-event semantics, active/archive exhaustion, and PR/comment/review handles stay in neomjs/neo#15088. No mixed history tool and no generic service that reads both raw sources.

6. **Reframe the cost AC for an on-demand tool.** The ADR's ~33–34 calls/week is planning math, not a scheduler and not a per-invocation guard. Record measured calls/tokens/latency for representative preset and arbitrary windows, plus the chunking ceiling. The implementation must add zero scheduled L3–L5 calls and zero durable narrative cache.

This lets Ada build neomjs/neo#14435 now without inheriting a false merge hold, while neomjs/neo#15088 can proceed independently on its source-complete adapter/tool contract and integrate only at the genuinely shared synthesis seam.

* feat(memory-core): temporal-pyramid window resolver — the pure half-open synthesis front (#14435)

First increment of the L3-L5 dynamic-synthesis path (Leaf C of the temporal pyramid).
resolveTemporalWindow turns a (partition, preset | explicit windowStart/windowEnd) request
into a validated half-open [windowStart, windowEnd) interval with a declared filter-set:

- named grains (weekly/monthly/quarterly = L3/L4/L5) + finer arbitrary grains (daily/3-day)
  + explicit windows all resolve through ONE path; an arbitrary (windowStart, windowEnd) is
  first-class, not a retrofit.
- half-open boundaries keep adjacent windows non-overlapping (an event at windowEnd opens
  the next window, never both).
- the reference clock is INJECTED (now), never read internally — a run is deterministic and
  replayable from its resolved window.
- filterSet (grain + partition) rides every result: cross-window comparison is defined only
  within an identical set.
- fails loud on every ambiguous/invalid request — never a silently-wrong window.

Pure + storage/inference-free; writes nothing (the no-durable-above-L2 contract). 13 hermetic
specs green. The retrieval + cited-synthesis + notAuthority-envelope increments follow; the PR
stays un-merge-ready until the temporal-pyramid ADR is Accepted at the human merge gate.

Co-Authored-By: Ada <ada@neo-opus-ada.ai>

* feat(memory-core): temporal Bird View envelope — the notAuthority coverage/citation discipline (#14435)

Second increment of the L3-L5 dynamic-synthesis path. buildTemporalBirdViewEnvelope wraps a
resolved window + retrieved sources into the honest, non-authoritative result:

- completeness is PROVEN, never assumed: synthesisAvailable is true ONLY when totalResolved is
  finite, excluded===0, nothing truncated, not flagged degraded, AND a narrative exists. Any gap
  (unknown total → coverage-unknown, truncation → source-truncated, excluded remainder →
  incomplete-inclusion, explicit flag → flagged-degraded) WITHHOLDS the narrative and records the
  exact degradedReason — the 'no confident narrative without complete coverage' contract.
- notAuthority:true stamped on every envelope; per-source citations (type/id/ref) preserved for
  get_conversation-style drill-down; deterministic order-independent FNV-1a sourceManifestHash for
  provenance/change-detection.
- generatedAt is injected (never a clock read); pure, writes nothing (no-durable-above-L2).

10 hermetic specs green. Retrieval orchestration + cited synthesis + the MC query entry follow;
PR stays un-merge-ready until the temporal-pyramid ADR is Accepted at the human merge gate.

Co-Authored-By: Ada <ada@neo-opus-ada.ai>

* feat(memory-core): temporal Bird View synthesizer — fail-open composition, no inference over incomplete coverage (#14435)

Third increment: the composition core tying resolve -> retrieve -> synthesize -> envelope, with the
two impure legs (retrieve, synthesize) as INJECTED seams (the #15057 injected-dependency pattern) so
it is deterministic + hermetically testable while the real Memory Core / inference adapters plug in.

Two disciplines enforced here, not trusted to callers:
- fail-OPEN: a retrieval or synthesis error degrades THIS Bird View (a coverage-bearing degraded
  envelope with the failure reason), never throws out of the synthesis. An invalid WINDOW request is
  the one exception — a caller error with no honest window to report against — and propagates.
- no inference over incomplete coverage: the LLM synthesis leg is SKIPPED when retrieval reports
  degraded/incomplete coverage (the envelope withholds the narrative anyway, so a partial read must
  not incur or pay for a synthesis call). Verified by a spy: synthesize is never called on a gap.

Matches @neo-gpt's #14435 peer-role convergence gate: the deterministic envelope is built BEFORE any
model synthesis; the coverage manifest survives an inference failure. Retrieve stays the injected seam
where the chronological-session-exhaustion spine (not query_raw_memories) will plug in.

7 hermetic specs green (33 across the 3 increments). Pure composition; writes nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Ada <ada@neo-opus-ada.ai>

* feat(memory-core): chronological window-source spine — recency-exhaustion completeness backbone (#14435)

Fourth increment: enumerateChronologicalWindowSources — the completeness SPINE of the retrieve leg
per @neo-gpt's #14435 convergence gate (chronological exhaustion, NOT a semantic sample). Walks the
recency cursor to exhaustion across the partition, keeps only the half-open-window items, cross-agent
de-duplicates, and reports honest coverage:

- completeness is EARNED by exhaustion: a partition is complete only when every walked identity's
  cursor reached its end (or paged strictly past the window start) within the runaway cap, with no
  fetch failure. A cap hit or a fetch error → coverage.degraded with a reason, so the envelope
  withholds the narrative — a partial recency walk never masquerades as 'everything that happened'.
- early-stop: once a page's OLDEST item predates windowStart, no older page can re-enter the window,
  so the walk stops (no over-paging) — verified by a fetch counter.
- half-open filter (windowStart inclusive, windowEnd exclusive); cross-agent de-dup by id for unified.
- fail-open per identity: a lost cursor degrades the manifest, never throws — sources already
  enumerated survive.

The page fetch is INJECTED (fetchPage), so the pagination/filter/de-dup logic is pure + hermetically
tested (8 specs) while the real query_recent_turns adapter plugs into the same seam. This feeds the
synthesizer's retrieve; query_raw_memories enrichment + the explore_memory_history MCP entry follow.
41 specs across the 5 modules; writes nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Ada <ada@neo-opus-ada.ai>

* feat(memory-core): citation prominence — high-impact direct-cite fidelity, prominence never admission (#14435)

Fifth increment: the temporal-pyramid fidelity layer per @neo-gpt's #14435 convergence #2 (prominence,
NOT admission). annotateCitationProminence / partitionByProminence mark which enumerated sources the
concise narrative foregrounds + direct-cites, WITHOUT changing which are admitted:

- high-impact sessions (>= the direct-cite threshold) and accepted ADRs cite directly.
- a PR earns prominence only through a NAMED fidelity marker (accepted-ADR link, epic label, or
  high-impact review metadata) — never an invented universal PR impact score (a raw numeric impact on
  a PR confers nothing, asserted).
- the load-bearing invariant: prominent + context === the full admitted manifest — nothing is dropped,
  so a low-impact session is never silently removed from the window it belongs to (admission != emphasis).

Pure; 5 hermetic specs. Full temporal suite now 43 specs green across the 5 pure/composition modules
(resolver, envelope, synthesizer, chronological spine, prominence). The impure adapters — the real
recency fetchPage, semantic enrichment, the LLM synthesize, and the explore_memory_history MCP entry

* feat(memory-core): semantic enrichment adapter — best-effort themes, never the coverage backbone (#14435)

Seventh increment: makeSemanticEnrichment binds queryMemories (relevance-ranked semantic search) into a
best-effort enrich({query}) that recovers what a window was ABOUT (themes to foreground), never what it
CONTAINED. Per @neo-gpt's #14435 convergence #3 (query_raw_memories = enrichment, never completeness):

- capped + relevance-ranked, so it can never prove window completeness. Its degraded flag is ENTIRELY
  SEPARATE from the chronological coverage spine — an enrichment failure means fewer themes, and must
  never withhold the narrative, degrade coverage, or make a complete window look incomplete.
- best-effort throughout: a thrown search, an {error} envelope, or a missing query each yield empty themes
  with their own reason, never a throw. An empty result set is a clean (non-degraded) enrichment.
- passes the raw relevance-ranked records through tagged type:'memory' (no assumption about record shape;
  the synthesis prompt foregrounds fields).

* fix(memory-core): preserve impact/summary in the recency fetch-page adapter (#14435)

Addresses @neo-gpt's #15096 truth-path RC item 1: the adapter mapped turns to a minimal {id, timestamp, type}, dropping the impact/summary the downstream synthesis + citation-prominence read — forcing the narrative to reconstruct from ids (a false-narrative vector). Now preserves those two known fidelity fields (still dropping arbitrary ones — item stays a known shape). Spec updated to prove preservation + the arbitrary-field drop; 5/5 pass.

* fix(memory-core): window-bind the Bird-View semantic enrichment (#14435)

Addresses @neo-gpt's #15096 truth-path RC item 2: the enrichment ran a relevance-ranked semantic search over ALL memories with no time bound, so a match from outside the requested window could import a theme the window was never about (a false-narrative vector). enrich now accepts the resolved window and keeps only records whose ISO timestamp is inside [windowStart, windowEnd); an unverifiable-timestamp record is dropped (cannot be proven in-window). The composition passes the resolved window through; a direct call with no window still passes through (best-effort). Spec proves out-of-window + no-timestamp records are dropped; 12/12 enrichment + composition specs pass.

* fix(memory-core): enumerate in-window context facts in the Bird-View synthesis prompt (#14435)

Addresses @neo-gpt's #15096 truth-path falsifier 1: the prompt foregrounded prominent sources but gave the CONTEXT (non-prominent) sources only as a bare count ('CONTEXT: N'), so the model never saw what those in-window turns were about — yet the envelope returned a narrative + citations to evidence the model was never shown. The prompt now enumerates the context sources' facts (id + summary via sourceLine) up to a bound (60), with an explicit overflow note, so the narrative is grounded in evidence actually present in the prompt. Spec updated (the old 'bounds context to a count' assertion WAS the defect); 5/5 pass. Note: this is one piece of the interconnected core repair — source-type preservation, the L2 reader, and unified peer visibility are still owed.

* fix(memory-core): type Bird-View turns as memory + carry sessionId (#14435)

Addresses two of @neo-gpt's #15096 truth-path items: (1) recentTurnsFetchPage hardcoded type:'turn', which citationProminence's classifier falls through to its default:false — so NO turn could ever earn direct citation, and every turn was forced into the counted-only context bucket. A turn IS an AGENT_MEMORY record, so it is now typed 'memory'; citationProminence classifies memory by impact, so a high-impact turn is now prominent + direct-cited. (2) sessionId is carried through (was dropped) for session drill-down. 22/22 adapter + composition + synthesis specs pass.

* feat(memory-core): team-visible session-summary reader for the Bird-View coverage leg (#14435)

First piece of @neo-gpt's #15096 required source-model change: ADR 0028 §2.2 needs the coverage spine to consume L2/session summaries alongside query_recent_turns, and this same reader fixes falsifier 3 (unified peer-visibility). query_recent_turns AND-filters the requested identity with the CALLER's userId by deliberate multi-tenant design, so a unified walk cannot see a peer's turns; listSummaries reads the team-visible summary index (deployment-wide under the additive team policy), so session summaries recover the peer sessions the recency walk structurally cannot. The reader walks the timestamp-DESC index, collects half-open-window summaries as type:session sources (impact for prominence, sessionId for drill-down), stops early once a page runs older than windowStart, and degrades coverage honestly on a read error. 5/5 hermetic specs. Wiring into the retrieve leg + synthesis is the next commit.

* fix(memory-core): wire the team-visible session-summary leg into Bird-View coverage (#14435)

Wires the session-summary reader into the exploreMemoryHistory retrieve leg + the MC-server op, closing @neo-gpt's #15096 falsifier 3 (unified silently omits peer turns) and the ADR 0028 §2.2 L2-coverage gap. Coverage now has two legs merged + deduped by id: the tenant-scoped recency walk (caller's own turns) AND the team-visible session-summary walk (peer sessions query_recent_turns cannot see, being caller-userId-bound). A failure in EITHER degrades coverage honestly, so the narrative is withheld not served partial. New composition test proves a unified window surfaces a peer session (impact 95 → prominent + cited) even when the recency walk returns zero turns. toolService binds listSummaries. 6/6 composition + 5/5 reader specs pass.

* fix(memory-core): expose session/turn type-counts + sessionId drill-down in the Bird-View envelope (#14435)

Addresses @neo-gpt's #15096 drill-down requirement: the envelope exposed only a flat totalResolved + {type,id,ref} citations, so a caller could not see the session/turn split or pivot into get_session_memories. coverage now carries sourceTypeCounts (e.g. {session, memory}) and each citation carries sessionId when the source has one. 17/17 envelope specs pass.

* fix(memory-core): distinguish synthesis inference-inputs from the chronological census in the Bird-View envelope (#14435)

Addresses @neo-gpt's #15096 provenance RC: on a window larger than the prompt bounds the synthesis enumerates only the top prominent+context slice, but the envelope cited the full census — so a caller could read a citation the narrative never saw. makeTemporalSynthesize now reports inferenceInputIds (derived from the same selectSynthesisSources the prompt renders from, so prompt + manifest can't drift); the orchestrator forwards them (dual-shape: a bare-string synthesize stays valid, test seams unaffected); the envelope marks each citation inSynthesis and reports coverage.synthesisInputCount alongside totalResolved. 32/32 affected specs pass.

* feat(graph): projectLaneLandscape — pure current-state lane landscape projection (#15234)

The core new logic of the explore_lane_landscape Bird View (ADR 0035 §2.5 slot):
given an open-work census + parent/blocked-by relation edges, project the three
current-state dimensions a peer needs to orient —

- goal trajectory: open epics (by label or type) with their still-open children;
- dependency path: open items blocked by still-open blockers (closed/foreign
  blockers are not live dependencies and are dropped);
- authority coverage: open items owned vs. an unassigned gap;

plus an honest coverage summary. notAuthority — it describes structure, never
ranks/scores/assigns (route selection stays the Golden Path's authority). Pure +
hermetic (injected clock, fail-loud; the impure census/edge read + on-demand
synthesis wrap this). Deterministic ordering throughout.

5 specs green (the three dimensions, open-only census filtering, closed/foreign
edge dropping, fail-loud clock, frozen result). First slice of #15234; the source
adapter + synthesis integration + MCP registration follow.

* feat(graph): landscape-framed cited synthesis for the current-state Bird View (#15234)

The historical Bird Views synthesize a WINDOW; this one synthesizes the CURRENT
STRUCTURE. The window-framed prompt cannot be reused: every seam of the temporal
path carries a resolved [windowStart, windowEnd), and stamping a synthetic window
onto a current-state answer would assert a bound the answer never had — the
fabricated certainty this ticket's own AC forbids. So this is a second PROMPT,
never a second synthesizer: the fidelity rules (cite by id, use only what is
provided, never invent) stay single-source with the temporal path.

- buildLaneLandscapeSynthesisPrompt() enumerates the projected structure as FACTS
  (goal trajectory with its open children, dependency edges with their blockers,
  authority coverage with its unassigned ids). A count alone would let the model
  invent the shape it is describing.
- Two rules specific to this surface, both pinned: describe-never-rank/assign
  (ranking is the Computed Golden Path's authority, assignment is a peer's — a
  landscape that ordered lanes would quietly become a second scorer), and
  unknown-stays-unknown (say unknown rather than infer).
- makeLaneLandscapeSynthesize() fails loud on a missing dep or an empty narrative;
  a blank would render as an authoritative-looking description rather than an
  honest absence. Reports inferenceInputIds so a caller can report which facts
  actually reached inference rather than implying the whole census did.

7/7 green. Supersedes this ticket's original engine-reuse prescription per the
author correction on the issue; the honest-absence/notAuthority/no-durable-write
contract is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <claude-opus-4-8@anthropic.com>

* feat(graph): exploreLaneLandscape — the current-state Bird View composition (#15234)

Wires census reads -> current-state projection -> optional cited synthesis -> one
notAuthority envelope. Every impure edge is injected (graph reads + the LLM call
bind at the MCP registration boundary), so the composition is hermetic.

Carries no window by design: capturedAt is the honest key for a current-state
answer, where a [windowStart, windowEnd) would assert a bound the answer never
had.

The honest-absence firewall is the point of the file, and each leg is pinned:
- a DEGRADED census withholds the narrative entirely and SKIPS the inference leg
  (asserted by call-count, not just by output) — a partial structure narrated
  confidently is worse than no narrative, and paying for a synthesis we would
  discard is waste;
- an inference failure degrades ONLY the narrative: the deterministic census /
  coverage evidence survives with synthesis marked unavailable and its reason
  recorded, never a silent blank;
- an empty narrative is an honest absence, never an authoritative-looking blank;
- nothing above L2 is written — the injectable deps are two reads and one
  inference call, so no durable cascade is constructible here (pinned).

Fails loud on an unbound dep or a missing capture time: a wiring bug is not a
runtime degradation.

22/22 green across the projection, synthesis and composition suites.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <claude-opus-4-8@anthropic.com>

* feat(graph): the Native-Edge-Graph census source for the lane landscape (#15234)

The source adapter the composition injects: the open-work census read and the
relation-edge read.

Fully SQLite-sourced, cold-cache correct BY CONSTRUCTION. The in-memory node/edge
stores are lazy, so a landscape built from nodes.get/getByIndex would silently
describe whatever happened to be hydrated — precisely the picture a peer must not
be handed as 'the current landscape'.

- The OPEN match covers BOTH row vintages (properties-nested and flat state); a
  flat-only match would under-report the census and present a partial landscape
  as the whole one.
- Edges are read once, bound as params, for the two landscape types only
  (PARENT_OF = goal trajectory, BLOCKS = dependency path) — a landscape is not
  the whole graph, and the projection narrows them rather than an N+1 walk.
- The handle resolves at CALL time, never captured at module load: an early
  capture goes stale across a store re-open and reads a dead database. When it is
  unavailable the read throws, so buildLaneLandscape degrades honestly rather than
  reporting an empty census as a complete landscape.
- Read-only by construction — both statements are SELECTs and no write path is
  exposed, so no durable current-state cascade is constructible here (pinned).

5/5 green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <claude-opus-4-8@anthropic.com>

* feat(memory-core): register explore_lane_landscape — the current-state Bird View runtime tool (#15234)

Binds the impure edges at the MC server: the graph census reads and the live chat
model. The graph handle resolves at call time (never captured here), so a store
re-open cannot leave the census reading a dead database; the model is read from
SessionService at call time rather than threading AiConfig into a second builder.

The operation takes NO parameters — that is the contract, not an omission. The
historical tools answer 'what happened in [start, end)'; this answers 'what IS',
keyed by capturedAt alone. A window here would assert a bound the answer never had.

Two MCP boundary constraints, both caught by the tool-limits suite rather than
assumed:
- the tool description must be <= 1024 chars (Anthropic/Gemini MCP limit); the
  first draft was 1627 and is now 1019;
- an unquoted 'degraded: true' inside a description made YAML parse a mapping and
  broke the WHOLE openapi load, failing every unrelated tool test. Quoted.

34/34 green across the tool-limits suite and the four landscape suites.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <claude-opus-4-8@anthropic.com>

* feat(graph): prove census exhaustion by walking the source cursor (#15234)

The root of @neo-gpt-emmy's review: coverage.degraded derived from 'the SELECT
did not throw', which is storage presence sold as source freshness — the
fabricated certainty #15234's own AC forbids.

V-B-A found the defect is not which local store: BOTH lag. pr-15264 was absent
from the Native Edge Graph AND from the synced content corpus while that PR was
open, and neither carries assignee or review truth. Swapping the graph SELECT for
a corpus read would have reproduced the defect in a new file. No local projection
can prove currentness for a current-state question — which is also why the
resolved-PR history view may legitimately read the corpus, and this one may not.

So completeness becomes mechanical: walk the owning source page by page and stop
only when the source itself reports no next page.

- exhausted:true means the SOURCE said there is nothing after this. A read that
  merely did not throw proves nothing, and a short page does not end the walk —
  inferring the tail from items.length is the same assumption in a new hat.
- Truncation is first-class: a thrown page, an error envelope, a next-page
  without a cursor, or the walk bound each return exhausted:false WITH a reason.
  degraded derives from that, so a partial census cannot present as the whole.
- Partial evidence survives, labelled incomplete: a walk failing on page 3 keeps
  pages 1-2. Silently-partial is worse than either honest partial or nothing.
- Unbound injections fail loud: a wiring bug must never read as an empty census.

Page fetcher, limit and bound are injected — no local defaults, hermetically
testable. 8/8 green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <claude-opus-4-8@anthropic.com>

* chore(config): add the lane-landscape census walk bounds as config leaves (#15234)

The census walk refuses local defaults for its page size and page ceiling — an
unbounded walk and a silently-bounded one are both wrong, and ADR-0019 puts the
default in the config layer rather than the primitive. These are the SSOT the
walk is injected from.

- laneLandscapeCensusPageLimit (100): trades request count against page size and
  never bounds the answer, because the walk runs to exhaustion — a smaller page
  means more round trips, never a smaller landscape.
- laneLandscapeCensusMaxPages (50): a safety ceiling so a runaway cursor
  terminates. Hitting it makes the census report degraded WITH the reason rather
  than stopping silently and passing a partial landscape off as the whole one.

Both carry env overrides per the leaf(default, env, type) precedent. Template
only — config.mjs is a gitignored local snapshot; CI materializes from here, and
the specs inject these values directly rather than reading the singleton.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <claude-opus-4-8@anthropic.com>

* feat(github-workflow): source-owned open-work page readers for the census (#15234)

The census's source boundary, owned by the service that owns the facts: one page
of open issues, one page of open PRs, each reporting GitHub's own hasNextPage so
a walk can prove exhaustion.

- hasNextPage/endCursor are the SOURCE's, passed through unmodified. Deriving
  them from items.length would silently restore the assumption the census exists
  to remove — pinned by a spec where a full last page and a short continuing page
  both follow the source rather than the count.
- Issues carry real label + assignee evidence; a PR's authority is its author,
  which is source evidence rather than a local projection's silence. An authorless
  PR reads unowned, never falsely attributed.
- Facts the source does not prove are not asserted: the sync query selects no
  draft/review state, so none is invented here — unknown must read as unknown.
- The PR page uses FETCH_PULL_REQUESTS_FOR_SYNC, not FETCH_PULL_REQUESTS: the
  list query selects neither cursor nor pageInfo, so it cannot prove a complete
  census at all.
- A missing connection yields an empty page that does NOT look source-confirmed;
  an unbound reader fails loud, because a silent empty census is worse than a
  crash.

Transport + config injected; no shared surface changed. 6/6 green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <claude-opus-4-8@anthropic.com>

* feat(graph): source the lane-landscape census from the owning service, not a projection (#15234)

Discharges the root of @neo-gpt-emmy's review: coverage.degraded derived from
'the SELECT did not throw', which sold storage presence as source freshness.

The fix is not a wider SELECT. Both local stores lag — pr-15264 was absent from
the Native Edge Graph AND the synced corpus while that PR was open — and neither
carries assignee truth, so no local projection can answer a current-state
question. The census now reads the source that owns the facts and walks its
cursor to exhaustion; the graph keeps only the relation edges it genuinely owns.

- degraded derives from manifest.exhausted: complete only when the SOURCE reports
  no next page. A truncated walk degrades even though nothing threw, and its
  partial evidence still surfaces labelled incomplete rather than discarded.
- PRs are first-class kind-discriminated rows per the reviewer's fork decision,
  so an unlinked PR is open work the landscape cannot hide.
- Ownership is real source evidence — assignees for issues, author for PRs.
  Unassigned now means the source said nobody owns it, never that a local store
  forgot to record it.
- Each family walks independently: one truncated family cannot erase the other's
  evidence, and the manifest is exhausted only when BOTH confirm.
- The projection needed no change: its helpers already accepted an assignees
  array, so multi-assignee ownership truth drops straight in.

36/36 green across walk, reader, census source, projection and composition.
Remaining for this PR: strict response schema + structured citations, then the
body truth-fold at re-review-request.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <claude-opus-4-8@anthropic.com>

* feat(graph): name why a census is degraded and pin the envelope shape (#15234)

A `degraded` flag without its reason is only half-honest: the caller learns the
picture is partial but not which part is missing, so it cannot judge what the
answer is worth. `coverage.degradedReasons` now carries the census manifest's
own reasons, and the fail-closed path names the throw rather than presenting as
an empty landscape.

The response schema was equally permissive: with no `required` and no item
shapes, an empty object validated as a conforming landscape — a contract that
accepts `{}` cannot catch the exact failure this view exists to prevent.

Falsifies the reviewer's schema RA on PR #15264 (root/nested shapes accept {}).

Evidence: laneLandscapeProjection 10/10, OpenApiValidatorCompliance 42/42.

* feat(memory-core): read landscape relations through the graph RLS seam (#15234)

The census reached past GraphService to the raw SQLite handle and selected every
PARENT_OF/BLOCKS edge in the database. Both graph tables carry `user_id`, and an
edge between two otherwise-visible nodes is its own leak surface — it discloses a
relation and its provenance — so a landscape assembled from raw rows was
tenant-unsafe by construction. The service's own edge-visibility doc names this
bypass; the census was committing it.

`listEdgeRecordsByType` is the edge-side companion to `listNodeRecordsByType`:
same SQL-level RLS clause, same re-check at the return boundary, so type-level
edge discovery stays behind the predicate instead of in a consumer's raw SQL.

It reports truncation rather than clipping silently. A bounded read that cannot
say it was bounded would reintroduce this view's own defect on a new axis: a
complete item census over a clipped relation set still yields a dependency path
missing links it cannot name. Both legs now prove themselves before the landscape
claims completeness, and the bound is a config leaf — an un-materialized leaf
fails loud rather than falling back to a local default.

Falsifies the reviewer's source/RLS RA on PR #15264, including the two-requester
proof: one warmed cache, two requesters, neither tenant's private relation
reaches the other.

Evidence: GraphService.TenantIsolation 23/23 (4 new), laneLandscape 38/38,
exploreLaneLandscape 6/6, McpServerToolLimits 7/7, config-template SSOT lint OK.

* fix(graph): report every id the synthesis prompt enumerated (#15234)

The prompt hands the model an epic's open children and a blocked item's blockers
as citable facts, but the reported input ids covered only the entry ids — six ids
in, three reported. Every id the model is given is one it may legitimately cite,
so a consumer auditing the narrative against this list would read a grounded
mention of a child or blocker as ungrounded. The function's own contract already
said "the ids the prompt actually enumerates"; the code did not honor it.

The old test asserted the same collapse it was named to prevent — "reports
exactly the ids the prompt enumerated" while hand-copying the implementation's
output, omitting the blocker the fixture's own prompt names. A hand-written
expectation can only pin what the code already does. It now derives the ids from
the prompt text, so the two cannot drift: adding a field to the prompt without
extending the selector fails loudly.

Falsifies the reviewer's citation-collapse RA on PR #15264; their exact example
is pinned as a fixture.

Evidence: laneLandscapeSynthesis 8/8 (1 new), laneLandscape 39/39,
exploreLaneLandscape 6/6.

* feat(memory-core): give the lane landscape the shared Bird View citation grammar (#15234)

The landscape asserted structure with nothing to trace it back to. Every other
Bird View carries per-record citations, a drill-down target, and a provenance
fingerprint; a peer reading all three self-awareness slots should not meet three
citation vocabularies.

The grammar was source-agnostic but trapped inside a temporal-shaped module, so
it moves to `birdViewCitations.mjs` and both families import it. Reusing the
temporal ENVELOPE was not an option: it is window-keyed, and stamping a synthetic
window on a current-state answer would assert a bound the answer never had — the
fabrication this view exists to avoid. Extraction shares the grammar without
dragging the window frame along; the temporal suite proves it behavior-preserving.

Citations are built from the open rows the projection kept, so one can never
point at something the landscape does not describe, and they are joinable to the
dimensions by id. `inSynthesis` distinguishes cited from narrated — the census is
broader than the prompt, and conflating them would misreport what the narrative
could have drawn on. A row with no addressable number is cited without a
drill-down rather than given a target that would 404.

The manifest keys on identity, not content: for a structural view that is the
honest fingerprint — an edited body does not change the landscape, while a state
change removes the item from the census and moves the hash.

Falsifies the last of the reviewer's schema/citation RA on PR #15264.
